query: From the Python zipfile source only, what are the requirements and exceptions for writing a ZIP archive into an in-memory binary buffer using writestr and ZipInfo, deterministic timestamps, closing to finalize the directory, and portable compression? verified_findings.finding: writestr accepts bytes or UTF-8 text; explicit ZipInfo carries date/time; a string name uses current time.
verified_findings.adoption: Fixed timestamp, explicit member identities and sorted parts; assert identical bytes on repeated export.

verified_findings.finding: Closing writes essential archive records; ZIP_STORED avoids optional compression modules.
verified_findings.adoption: Context-managed ZIP_STORED archive; reopen and resolve every required part.
